lit.\u0027\u003cb\u003ec = λ·f\u003c/b\u003e: "c = λ·f: as f increases, λ decreases."
lit.\u0027\u003cb\u003eE = hf\u003c/b\u003e:: "E = hf: higher frequency, more energy per photon."
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl espectro va de las:
"

The spectrum runs from radio waves (λ > 1 m) to γ rays (λ < 10 pm). Here it is traversed on a logarithmic scale: as λ decreases, f and E increase. The yellow arrows are the Poynting vector S = E × B/μ₀, which indicates the energy flow.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn la luz \u003cb\u00:
"

In linear light E oscillates in a plane. In circular light the tip of E describes a helix; the sense is defined looking toward the source. Chiral molecules absorb left and right circular light differently (circular dichroism). The test charge shows that E accelerates it.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa energía llega en \:
"

Energy comes in quanta. The smaller the λ, the greater the energy per photon: E(eV) = 1239.84/λ(nm). The localized wave packet represents one photon; the total intensity depends on the number of photons, not on the energy of each.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eRadio: espines nuclea:
"

Radio: nuclear spins (NMR). Microwaves: rotations. IR: vibrations. Visible and UV: electronic transitions. X-rays and γ: ionization and nuclear transitions. With ≳ 10 eV a photon can remove valence electrons (IE of H = 13.6 eV).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eUn campo eléctrico \u:
"

An electric field E and a magnetic field B regenerate each other. They are transverse, in phase and travel at c = 299,792,458 m/s in a vacuum. The animation uses a compressed visual λ (logarithmic scale).

"

lit.\u0027Excita rotaciones moleculares. En: "It excites molecular rotations. In polar molecules such as H₂O the dipole tries to align with the oscillating field; friction between molecules heats (microwave oven, 2.45 GHz)."
lit.\u0027Excita vibraciones de enlace (esti: "It excites bond vibrations (stretching and bending). Basis of IR spectroscopy (≈ 4000–400 cm⁻¹): O–H ≈ 3300 cm⁻¹, C=O ≈ 1700 cm⁻¹. It is perceived as heat."
lit.\u0027Ioniza y arranca electrones intern: "It ionizes and removes inner electrons. Its λ (≈ 0.1 nm) is comparable to interatomic distances, which is why it is diffracted by crystals (crystallography). It passes through soft tissue."

lit.\u0027Mueve los electrones libres de los: "It moves the free electrons in conductors (currents in antennas). Its energy is much lower than k_BT: it neither excites nor breaks bonds. In NMR, from 60 to 900 MHz it flips nuclear spins inside an intense magnetic field."
lit.\u0027Perspectiva, plano E, plano B y fr: "Perspective, E plane, B plane and front."
lit.\u0027Promueve electrones de valencia en: "It promotes valence electrons between orbitals (π→π*, d–d transitions). It gives rise to the color of compounds and the photochemistry of vision and photosynthesis."
lit.\u0027Recorre el espectro de las ondas d: 'Sweep the spectrum from radio waves to gamma rays: λ falls and the photon energy rises (E = hf).'
lit.\u0027Se originan en transiciones nuclea: "They originate in nuclear transitions and annihilation. They penetrate deeply, ionize and, above 1.022 MeV, can produce e⁻/e⁺ pairs."
lit.\u0027Son transversales, en fase, y |E|: "They are transverse, in phase, and |E| = c·|B|."
lit.\u0027Transiciones electrónicas de mayor: "Higher-energy electronic transitions. UV-C (< 280 nm) breaks bonds (DNA damage, photolysis of O₃) and, toward the extreme UV (< ≈ 124 nm, > 10 eV), it ionizes."
